source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
PIT2 publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 47,100 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, the same power supports around 500 racks. The operator has not published a rack count, a power density figure, or a cooling specification, so which of those numbers applies here is not determinable from the published data.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no reading of what workloads those certifications qualify the campus to host is possible from the data.

Within Pennsylvania, this site has the second-highest published IT capacity among the facilities this site has read, at 5 MW of the 11 MW total published across two facilities. Fourteen Pennsylvania facilities are mapped overall, but twelve of those publish no megawatt figure, meaning the state picture is incomplete. A campus that ranks second in a two-facility published sample is a meaningful local presence, but it is a small footprint by the standards of AI training infrastructure, where single hyperscale deployments routinely exceed this campus's total capacity by an order of magnitude.
